texts.orig: The TOE  is a Secure Element which can be used as a Trustable System-on-Chip (TSoC) for providing cryptographic services to a secure connected IOT device. The iMQ SQ713x series platform IC is built on iMQ's proprietary 16-bit CPU core, the 870E, derived from Toshiba's 8-bit TLCS-870/C1 core. The 870E core retains the same instruction set architecture (ISA) as the 870C1. However, its internal general-purpose registers, as well as the address, instruction, and data buses, have been upgraded from 8-bit to 16-bit. The usage and security features of the SE is further described in section 1.5.3.
texts.text: The TOE  is a Secure Element which can be used as a Trustable System-on-Chip (TSoC) for providing cryptographic services to a secure connected IOT device. The iMQ SQ713x series platform IC is built on iMQ's proprietary 16-bit CPU core, the 870E, derived from Toshiba's 8-bit TLCS-870/C1 core. The 870E core retains the same instruction set architecture (ISA) as the 870C1. However, its internal general-purpose registers, as well as the address, instruction, and data buses, have been upgraded from 8-bit to 16-bit. The usage and security features of the SE is further described in section 1.5.3.

texts.text: The proposed TOE is composed of hardware design, embedded firmware, and guidance documents:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig:  Hardware: iMQ SQ713x series IC is the secure element dedicated for network security and authentication. iMQ proprietary Trust Computing Engine, hereinafter will be referred to as 'iMQ_TCE," is a physical hardware implemented design with high security strength compliant with NIST standard FIPS 140-3 level 3. iMQ_TCE_V1_06 hardware design includes hash, symmetric and asymmetric cryptographic algorithms, secure boot loader as well as anti-tamper physical layer protection. The relevant security function claimed in [Datasheet] section 3.3.

The relevant security function claimed in [Datasheet] section 3.3.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig:  Embedded firmware: iMQ specific firmware stack and crypto library are tailored for encryption/decryption application. iMQ_FW_2_1_00 software design includes iMQ proprietary secure boot, command handler and self-test on health as well as exception and zeroization procedure.

texts.orig: The logical scope of the platform is illustrated within the red box of Figure 2. The logical scope includes: SE Hardware (V1.06) and Firmware (V2.1.00). The scope for the Security evaluation is the combination of the trusted hardware and firmware components implementing a secure element environment with the Security Functional Requirements stated in this document. The SQ713x secure element includes the embedded firmware 'iMQ_FW' and the circuit implemented cryptographic accelerator 'iMQ_TCE.' The secure boot loader is bundled in the iMQ_TCE design to check the digest from firmware image. Within iMQ_FW, the major two portions are a compact 'Crypto Library' which is based on the supported cryptographic algorithms in iMQ_TCE and a proprietary 'Command Parser' used to handle the command request from platform host. The security functions built inside iMQ_FW are only accessible if the data of firmware passes the integrity validation by boot loader during startup. If the validation fails during the boot stage, subsequent command requests from platform host will be rejected by iMQ_FW, which instead returns an error status.

texts.orig: iMQ has defined a Software and Hardware Security Incident Response Procedure (SHSIRP), implemented by a dedicated team (Technical Support). This process provides a publicly available interface (https://www.imqtech.com/en/tools/pss) and includes 4 steps:
texts.text: iMQ has defined a Software and Hardware Security Incident Response Procedure (SHSIRP), implemented by a dedicated team (Technical Support). This process provides a publicly available interface (https://www.imqtech.com/en/tools/pss) and includes 4 steps:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig:  Reporting. The process begins when Technical Support becomes aware of a potential security vulnerability in an iMQ product. Upon receiving a report, Technical Support provides an acknowledgment to the reporter and ensures timely updates throughout the investigation and resolution process.
texts.text:  Reporting. The process begins when Technical Support becomes aware of a potential security vulnerability in an iMQ product. Upon receiving a report, Technical Support provides an acknowledgment to the reporter and ensures timely updates throughout the investigation and resolution process.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig:  Evaluation. Technical Support evaluates the reported issue to confirm its validity, assesses associated risks, determines potential impacts, and assigns an appropriate processing priority. This step is critical to ensure that the response is proportionate to the threat level and product context.
texts.text:  Evaluation. Technical Support evaluates the reported issue to confirm its validity, assesses associated risks, determines potential impacts, and assigns an appropriate processing priority. This step is critical to ensure that the response is proportionate to the threat level and product context.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig:  Solution. Once the issue is confirmed, Technical Support collaborates with the relevant product teams to develop an appropriate mitigation strategy. The nature of the solution may vary depending on the type and severity of the vulnerability.

texts.orig: The platform ensures its authenticity and integrity during the platform initialization. If the platform authenticity or integrity cannot be ensured, the platform will enter a state where it cannot perform any other commands except responding to Info Command and providing information such as revision and error status.

texts.orig: The platform implements a robust secure initialization mechanism to ensure the authenticity and integrity of the execution environment during the boot phase. If firmware verification fails or the platform enters an abnormal state, a default security failure response is triggered-such as system reset, halt, or firmware erasure-to prevent execution of unauthorized or potentially malicious code.
texts.text: The platform implements a robust secure initialization mechanism to ensure the authenticity and integrity of the execution environment during the boot phase. If firmware verification fails or the platform enters an abnormal state, a default security failure response is triggered-such as system reset, halt, or firmware erasure-to prevent execution of unauthorized or potentially malicious code.

texts.label: text

Depending on the selected mode, the platform applies SHA256 hash or CRC16 algorithms, optionally combined with a 32-byte Boot Key and a device Unique Identifier (UID), to achieve the following functions:

texts.orig: The entropy sources are provided by the hard-macro, and the post-processing algorithm for random number generation is implemented by firmware and cryptographic operation. The platform implements random number generation by utilizing the True Random Number Generation capability of the security engine. Each TRNG request generates a 128-bit random number.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: TOE provides a complete key storage and usage protection mechanism to ensure that even if the key is stored within the platform, sensitive information will not be leaked due to access by applications or unauthorized entities.
texts.text: TOE provides a complete key storage and usage protection mechanism to ensure that even if the key is stored within the platform, sensitive information will not be leaked due to access by applications or unauthorized entities.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: TOE supports AES-128, AES-256, ECC-P256, and ECC-P384 encryption keys. The method of generating and importing keys depends on the type and usage scenario. For example, the ECC private key is randomly generated internally by the TOE based on the GenKey command sent by the Host and stored in a controlled secure area; while the AES key can be imported by the Host in plain text, encrypted format, or generated through the ECDH algorithm or KDF key derivation mechanism.
texts.text: TOE supports AES-128, AES-256, ECC-P256, and ECC-P384 encryption keys. The method of generating and importing keys depends on the type and usage scenario. For example, the ECC private key is randomly generated internally by the TOE based on the GenKey command sent by the Host and stored in a controlled secure area; while the AES key can be imported by the Host in plain text, encrypted format, or generated through the ECDH algorithm or KDF key derivation mechanism.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: All keys are stored in TOE's dedicated EEPROM or SRAM space, which has access restrictions and hardware isolation design. The host cannot read the key plaintext in any way and that can only be used in a controlled manner through an authorization mechanism.
texts.text: All keys are stored in TOE's dedicated EEPROM or SRAM space, which has access restrictions and hardware isolation design. The host cannot read the key plaintext in any way and that can only be used in a controlled manner through an authorization mechanism.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: To ensure the confidentiality and resistance against analysis of keys during storage, the TOE applies a scrambling process to the key content. The scrambling uses a random seed uniquely stored in NVR, ensuring that even when identical keys are stored on different chips, the actual data representation in memory differs. This further enhances security against physical attacks.
texts.text: To ensure the confidentiality and resistance against analysis of keys during storage, the TOE applies a scrambling process to the key content. The scrambling uses a random seed uniquely stored in NVR, ensuring that even when identical keys are stored on different chips, the actual data representation in memory differs. This further enhances security against physical attacks.

texts.orig: In addition, if the internal CPU needs to perform key import operations, this must be processed through a dedicated hardware encryption engine to ensure that the generation, input, storage and use of keys throughout their entire life cycle are completed within a trusted boundary, thereby achieving the goal of protecting the confidentiality and integrity of the keys.

texts.orig: The secure communication channel authenticates Host Platform and protects against disclosure, modification, replay, erasure of messages between the endpoints, using self-defined protocols and measures.
texts.text: The secure communication channel authenticates Host Platform and protects against disclosure, modification, replay, erasure of messages between the endpoints, using self-defined protocols and measures.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The TOE and the host application exchange session public keys, random nonce, and signatures. Based on these parameters and their respective private keys, a shared session key is generated. This key is used to protect the confidentiality (AES-256 CBC) and integrity (MAC) of data during secure communication. For more information, please refer to Section 11.1 "Authentication" and Section 11.2 "Secure Communication" in the [Datasheet].
